data.name: Events.HotkeyPressed.Name
data.value: Hotkey pressed

data.name: Events.HotkeyPressed.Description
data.value: Fires whenever a modifier and key combination is pressed anywhere on this machine.

data.name: Events.HotkeyPressed.Combo.Label
data.value: Hotkey

data.name: Events.HotkeyPressed.Combo.Description
data.value: The key that fires this trigger. Click Record and press the combo, or pick a key and toggle the modifiers. A key with no modifier is allowed - but a bare key such as a letter or digit then fires this trigger on every press of it anywhere on the machine, so use one only when that is what you want.

data.name: Events.HotkeyPressed.Suppress.Label
data.value: Also stop this key from reaching other apps

data.name: Events.HotkeyPressed.Suppress.Description
data.value: Optional. Keeps this combo's trailing key from reaching the focused app - useful when the key also does something there. Modifiers like Ctrl or Shift are never intercepted. On Linux your desktop asks once whether Macro Deck may take over the combo, and then keeps it from every app regardless of Device, Profile or Folder.

data.name: Events.HotkeyPressed.Device.Label
data.value: Device

data.name: Events.HotkeyPressed.Device.Description
data.value: Optional. Only fires while this exact device is connected. Add Profile or Folder too to mean this device in that profile or folder.

data.name: Events.HotkeyPressed.Device.Placeholder
data.value: Any device

data.name: Events.HotkeyPressed.Profile.Label
data.value: Profile

data.name: Events.HotkeyPressed.Profile.Description
data.value: Optional. Only fires while this profile is open on some connected device.

data.name: Events.HotkeyPressed.Profile.Placeholder
data.value: Any profile

data.name: Events.HotkeyPressed.Folder.Label
data.value: Folder

data.name: Events.HotkeyPressed.Folder.Description
data.value: Optional. Only fires while this folder is open on some connected device - bind the same combo once per folder so only the open one reacts.

data.name: Events.HotkeyPressed.Folder.Placeholder
data.value: Any folder

data.name: Issues.KeyboardAccessRequired.Title
data.value: System Hotkeys cannot see the keyboard

data.name: Issues.KeyboardAccessRequired.Description.MacOs
data.value: macOS has not allowed Macro Deck to read keyboard input, so no hotkey fires. Open System Settings, Privacy & Security, Input Monitoring and turn on Macro Deck. Hotkeys start working a few seconds later. If they do not, restart Macro Deck.

data.name: Issues.KeyboardAccessRequired.Description.Linux
data.value: Macro Deck cannot read any keyboard, so no hotkey fires. Add your user to the input group (sudo usermod -aG input $USER), then log out and back in. Hotkeys start working a few seconds after Macro Deck can read the keyboard. Until then only hotkeys set to stop their key from reaching other apps fire, through your desktop.

data.name: Issues.KeyboardAccessRequired.Action
data.value: Check again

data.name: Issues.KeyboardAccessRequired.StillDenied
data.value: Macro Deck still cannot read the keyboard.

data.name: Issues.AccessibilityRequired.Title
data.value: Hotkeys still reach other apps

data.name: Issues.AccessibilityRequired.Description
data.value: A hotkey trigger is set to stop its key from reaching other apps, which on macOS needs Accessibility access. Open System Settings, Privacy & Security, Accessibility and turn on Macro Deck. Until then, hotkeys still fire but the focused app sees the key too.

data.name: Issues.ShortcutsNotTaken.Title
data.value: Some hotkeys still reach other apps

data.name: Issues.ShortcutsNotTaken.Description
data.value: A hotkey trigger is set to stop its key from reaching other apps, but your desktop has not taken over that combo: it was declined, has no key in your desktop's shortcut settings, or your desktop does not offer global shortcuts to apps. Open the shortcut settings and give Macro Deck's shortcuts their keys. On a desktop without them, bind the combo to a command that does nothing (such as true) in its own shortcut settings. Until then, hotkeys still fire but the focused app sees the key too.

data.name: Issues.ShortcutsNotTaken.Action
data.value: Open shortcut settings

data.name: Issues.ShortcutsNotTaken.CannotOpen
data.value: Your desktop cannot open Macro Deck's shortcut settings. Assign the keys in its own shortcut settings, or bind the combo to a command that does nothing (such as true) there.

data.name: Shortcuts.Description
data.value: Macro Deck hotkey {combo}

data.name: Issues.Unknown
